newsitem.title: FINLAND: Mine highlights Finland's depleting metal resource.
newsitem.headline: Mine highlights Finland's depleting metal resource.

text.p: Finland's Pyhasalmi mine may face closure in the next few years, underscoring the country's diminishing mineral resources and mining giant Outokumpu Oy's recent troubles with base metals.

Mine officials at Pyhasalmi told visitors on Friday that the copper and zinc mine -- the only one of its kind in Finland -- could close by the end of the year 2000 unless planned exploration showed growth in the current reserves.
A gaping orange-streaked pit, partially filled with slag and situated near the operation's silos and concentrating facilities, testifies to Pyhasalmi's roots some 30 years ago as an open-pit mine.
But now all the mining is done by stoping underground to a depth of 1,070 meters. The pit features a cavernous ramp seven kilometers long and stretching to the depths of the pit.
"There's a project for expansion underground and the target for exploration is 1,080 to 1,300 meters," said Jaako Ahtiainen, manager of the mining department.
"Exploratory drilling should start in October, and a feasibility study will be done by April 1998 -- then we will be in a position to make a decision."

The mine produces about a million tonnes of ore annually which after floatation processing last year translated into 9,315 tonnes of copper in concentrate and 25,681 tonnes of zinc in concentrate, along with pyrite concentrate, and some gold and silver.
"Speaking globally, it's a low-grade orebody. We have to push hard to be profitable," Ahtianinen said, pegging copper content at 0.9 percent and zinc is at 1.9-2.0 percent.
Some analysts visiting the mine said extending the mine's life may end up being uneconomic.

"Outokumpu's base metal mining business has lost a lot of money and here's one of the reasons. Mining at 1,000 metres is not cheap. This is not an open pit mine in Chile," said Orjan Roden, an equities analyst at Sweden's Den Danske bank.
Analyst James May of Metal Bulletin Research, said copper and zinc prices are expected to drop by 2000, reducing the incentive to keep the mine running.

"Unless a major new deposit is found nearby, the Pyhasalmi mine will close," May said. "Base metal mining in Finland is dead and once Pyhasali closes Outokumpu's involvement in base metal mining in Finland will be essentially at an end."
